# Matthogg’s Payswords

*Pages PDF 72-83*

## ## Matthogg’s Payswords
## **From Mountainside to Forest’s Edge**
Matthogg’s Payswords are a company of Ogre Mercenaries that ply their trade across the Old World, fighting for whoever either pay or feed them well. The company has fought Orcs, Goblins, Beastmen, Dwarfs, and more than a few Humans. Most recently, and somewhat ruinously, Matthog led his company into the World’s Edge Mountains. 

There the Payswords became embroiled in a series of battles between the various Orc and Goblin tribes that infest the mountains. During the fighting, the Ogres would ultimately serve various sides. 

The Payswords acquitted themselves, if not honourably, then certainly with a talent for spectacular violence and gore. Now Matthogg’s Payswords are much reduced in number. Matthog has set up camp in Ostermark, within the shade of the eaves of Gryphon’s Wood and close to the town of Nagenhof. The forest has been picked clean of easy game, and a few famished Ogres have even taken to devouring the more tender-looking saplings. 

There is only so much fibre one requires, however, and for an Ogre, there is no substitute for meat. Matthogg knows that he must find new opportunities soon or face further desertions or outright rebellion. 

While banditry is always an option, Matthogg is set upon establishing a reputation for himself and the Payswords as mercenaries par excellence. Eating the potential clientele is not a good long-term strategy — especially when they might pay you to eat someone else. 

But Matthogg has overlooked the existence of powerful entities in the forests about. Spites and Dryads may not come into direct conflict with the Ogres (such creatures don’t make good eating for a start) but those who make their lair within the eaves of Gryphon’s Wood are turning increasing hostile eyes on the neighbouring Ogres, who chop down trees for timber for their cookfires, and let their monstrous mounts rove the woods in search of animals to chase, kill, and eat. 

MATTHOGG’S PAYSWORDS 

## **Disposition of the Payswords**
This list represents the mercenary company at its current strength at their forest camp. At any given time, at least some Ogres are out hunting meat or attempting to find work. The forest has been picked clean, however, and the company’s Skirmishers have resorted to raiding local farms for meat. So far, Matthogg is not aware of this activity, and the Skirmishers claim that the meat comes from ‘some kind o’ local skinny Rhinox’. 

## **Shield Design**
Ogres do not use shields. ‘A shield’s just a flimsy, flat club, ain’t it?’ is a common refrain. Instead, most favour enormous reinforced gutplates. Matthog wears a rusted iron plate bearing a design representing the Great Maw. Most of his warriors have daubed a similar design onto their own gutplates. 

## **Battlecry**
‘Meat!’ 

- Yrg Beastkiller, the best of the company’s Hunters (Skirmishers), is often to one side of the camp where she can be found carving fresh javelins from young birch trees. 

- A standing guard of four Ogres (Soldiers) led by Krag Gutspill (Elite) patrols the edge of the camp, carefully eyeing the forest in the direction of the road, lest a passing traveller whistle loudly enough to be plausibly considered a threat. 

- The company’s Butcher, Rulg Deathcheater (Shaman), is usually at the centre of the camp. He can be found either butchering a kill brought to him by the company’s Hunters, or deep in the forest devouring a pot of offal as a rite to the Great Maw. 

- The Big Top, as the Ogres call Matthogg’s tent, sits at the centre of the camp and usually contains Matthogg himself (Chief) and Skel Longstrider (Elite), typically during one of Skel’s many attempts to convince her commander to take a more aggressive approach to improving the fortunes of the Payswords. 

## Ogres and Templates
Tribes and Tribulations is focused on Orc and Goblin tribes, and closely related species. Ogres are included because their tribal structure has several simularities to that of Orcs and Goblins, and they have similar belligerant attitudes and poor appreciation of of things like technology, the finer aspects culture, peace treaties, and refraining from eating captives. However, Ogres differ from Orcs and Goblins in many ways. A full account of Ogre Characters, Careers, and weaponry can be found in **Archives of the Empire Volume 2** . 

Ogres do not use shields, however they may take Ironfists instead. Rules for Ironfists can be found in **Archives of the Empire Volume 2** . They can be counted as Bucklers. 

Ogre Hunters live alongside Ogre communities. They can be made using the Skirmisher Template. However they have _Ranged (Throwing)_ and three javelins rather than a bow or a sling. 

Ogre Ironguts are a type of heavily armed veteran warrior common to most large Ogre tribes. They can be made by applying the Elite template. 

Ogre Butchers can be made using the Shaman template. Some Ogre Butchers rise to the vaunted rank of Slaughtermaster, and can be made using the Shaman Lord template. They use a type of ritual magic known as Gut Magic. The other sort of Ogre spellcaster is the Firebelly, which uses the Lore of Fire. 

## **Uniform**
The Payswords have little that would pass for a uniform, but the Ogre tendency to adopt local dress and custom has led to most of them dressing in something approximating Reikland fashion; doublets with slashed sleeves, prominent plumes, and leather breeches. Only Rulg Deathcheater has eschewed this way of dressing, preferring a leather apron fashioned from the tanned hides of a dozen ‘donors’ he has butchered over the years. 

Ogre spellcasters use Toughness rather than Intelligence for the purpose of determining their Language (Magick) Skill, so swap the bonus for Intelligence with that of the bonus for Toughness when using a template to make an Ogre Butcher or Firebelly. 

Ogre leaders are often referred to as Bruisers or Tyrants, and use the Chief and Warlord templates respectively. 

## Olde Weirde’s Incunabulum
And in the ancient tomb of the Zharr Dwarf chieftain beset on all sides by ferocious cave Goblins, with Professor von Gronighof engulfed by the foul creatures, and Sovrissniz and Kaia fighting a desperate retreat, I became at once grateful, awed, and horrified, by the Ogres’ prowess in battle. 

We had joined a caravan winding its way through the World’s Edge Mountains, and then across the Plain of Zharr to the Mountains of Mourn. We had enjoyed the company and safety of the large caravan and would have been content to keep with it all the way to Cathay had Professor von Gronighof not become distracted by rumours of the mausoleum of an ancient chieftain overlooking a nearby mountain pass. We had become used to von Gronighof digging up the dead at every opportunity, and I could say that it was getting tiresome. However, the caravan went missing a few days later and was never heard of again. So I will concede that von Gronighof’s compulsion to visit one tomb kept us from our own. 

We were nervous to leave the caravan and venture off alone in such inhospitable and strange terrain. But I found a band of half a dozen Ogres who were escorting the caravan prepared to accompany us up to the tomb. Naturally, I had seen a number of Ogres on my travels, and even the odd one in Altdorf itself, but had never encountered one in the wild, so to speak. And I had never had to deal with one directly. Having ascertained their leader, a particularly large specimen called Thagonni Gutbuster, I proceeded to negotiate with her for their services. 

The first thing that struck me was her sheer size. Of course, Ogres are big, but it was only when I stood before one and attempted a conversation that I realised quite how large, hulking, intimidating, and overpowering they are. And here, in their homelands, they were not affecting the clothing and equipment of the Empire as they are wont to do when travelling there, but they were dressed in more traditional Ogre garb. Except for their colourful trousers, they had barely an inch of cloth on their body. 

Some strategic parts of their bodies were adorned with metal armour held on with leather straps, but most of their skin was left bare. This armour was sometimes well-fitting and suited to its task and sometimes ad hoc and improvised. 

Being not inclined to enter a discussion about the Ogre proclivity for smithing, I assumed that sometimes they had the money to commission this armour, perhaps from the local Dwarfs, and sometimes they merely ripped what they could from battlefield dead. 

Every Ogre, however, seemed to take special pride in one particular piece of armour, the large round plate that protected their bellies. This, they call, with a simplicity typical of their kind, the gut plate. I got the impression, as we negotiated, that Thagonni was presenting her stomach to me in much the same way that a gentleman farmer might present a prized bull, as a sort of testament to his expertise. 

So fond of food are the Ogres and so proud of their bellies, it makes sense, I suppose, that they were, to an Ogre, armoured with gut plates, and yet very few of them wear helmets. That, I suggest, is an indication of the relative values they place on eating and thinking. Many of these gut plates were fashioned with an icon, circular in nature and seemingly comprising many and varied sharp teeth. This is something they call the Great Maw. Though I did not question them further on this, I surmise it translates as something like ‘Grand Mother,’ and points to a culture of ancestor worship similar to that of the Dwarfs, and I wondered whether the Ogres could have picked this tradition up from the Dwarfs of Zharr. 

I was also struck by the slovenly and casual mien of the creatures, and their lack of manners, especially, their willingness to interrupt any part of negotiations with a snack, or more accurately perhaps, a feast. They seemed to be at a constant meal and spoke to me only between mouthfuls of meat and gulps of ale, often with their mouths full. I thought at first this must be my fault for interrupting their mealtime, but soon learned that any time for these Ogres was potentially mealtime. 

I was keen to share with them the details of our plans and some rudimentary background lore on the ancient civilisations of the area. But they were entirely uninterested in any of this. All they wished to know was whether the mission was dangerous and that there was the prospect of a good fight (which I assured them there was) and what we were willing to pay. 

I offered them a purse full of gold coins, which I understood to be the standard payment for Ogres. There was however some confusion. Not, I think, because they were not up to the intellectual appreciation of abstract currency, but because this band had not been to the Empire and were merely unaccustomed to Imperial coinage. 

MATTHOGG’S PAYSWORDS 

Kaia, rather smugly, asked whether she could be of some assistance, and beckoned to Thagonni, leading her to a nearby muleskinner. She went through the act of purchasing an ox from the fellow, with exaggerated gestures, and then presented Thagonni with the animal. She immediately appreciated the value, then, of Imperial coinage, and ripped the hind leg of the creature, stuffing it into her face in celebration. And negotiations paused once more while the entire band tucked into the unfortunate creature. 

A couple of days later, we arrived at the stark, mountainside tomb. Von Gronighof found some inscriptions that he said might be key in understanding the civilisation and Sovrissniz was able to help him with some elements of the translation despite her decidedly unacademic bent. They agreed the language was very similar to Khazalid and perhaps marked a moment shortly before the Dwarfs of Zharr fell. 

However, while von Gronighof was working on the intricate friezes that lined the tomb’s great hall, he managed to dislodge one of the keystones of the ancient structure and sent a portion of the wall crashing down. The din alerted a large tribe of cavedwelling Goblins who had made the mausoleum part of their underground domain. They flooded from the darkness and set upon us from all sides. If we had not had the Ogres with us, we would have undoubtedly perished. But they joined the foul cave dwellers with gusto, not just using their superior strength and size, but fighting with discipline and skill, and remarkable tactical appreciation. Or so Kaia explained to me afterwards. 

And when the battle was won, they proceeded to consume the bodies of the fallen Goblins. They didn’t seem that impressed with the taste but made sure to eat every one regardless, forcing them down like obedient children eating their greens. 

Professor Pfaff tried to negotiate a cut in their fee in the light of the free lunch, but they would not be moved, and I had to intercede before things turned nasty. 

Since that ill-fated trip into the Mountains of Mourn, I have encountered Ogres a good number of times. And of course, one does not need to travel that far to find these gluttonous mercenaries. I have met several bands in the Empire, and I have seen an Ogre walk down the Street of a Hundred Taverns with a feather in his hat like any Altdorf citizen. Those I have encountered closer to home seem much more inclined to the civilising influence of our Empire. 

For such a wild and unsophisticated species, they seem remarkably good at integrating into Imperial society (and, I suggest, other societies across the world), content to wear similar clothes to our soldiers, and to adopt the standards of our military. 

And away from the army, where they naturally band together into all-Ogre regiments, these creatures seem to get on well enough as individuals. A single Ogre, for that is much the easiest number to feed, can find respectable work throughout the Empire, labouring, bodyguarding, pit fighting, or even butchering, and I’m sure at less reputable work for someone who needs a strong sword arm or a heavy hand. But it is testament to this ability that they can walk with the poshest noble or the lowest criminal. 

The same could be said of their cuisine, too. As they are such gluttons and so unfussy that I have witnessed them gorge themselves upon cave Goblins fresh from the battle, it is surprising that those living among civilisation are able to appreciate finer cuisine. I have even heard of one mercenary group that refused to go on campaign unless accompanied by their favourite Halfling chef. Despite this, I’m sure it is safe to say, even the most sophisticated Ogre palate still prefers quantity over quality. 

So, despite their uncouth manner, and their ridiculous belligerence, the way these creatures have travelled to all corners of the known world, the way they are able to find their niche in these places, the way they can adapt to different terrain and climate, and cultures, puts me in mind of the greatest travellers, and the most learned academics. Their wanderlust and their restlessness, their ability to conform to other cultures, makes me think these creatures are more astute, more adaptive, and more intelligent than we ever give them credit for. 

## **Tactics**
Few would willingly engage a whole camp of Ogres, but such is the combined hunger and boredom of the rank and file that they’ll jump at any excuse for a fight and a meal. While Matthogg himself knows better than to antagonise the locals, he will join any fight once blood is in the air, knowing full well that attempting to hold back the Payswords is both foolish and boring. 

Despite the Ogres’ reputation for mindless savagery, the surviving Payswords are experienced warriors. While a contingent of the group mostly consisting of Soldiers charge an enemy head on, the Hunters attempt to flank their opponents to harass them from unexpected angles and cut off any retreat. 

Matthogg himself seeks the most dangerous looking opponent to face and ideally devour in single combat. The Butcher Rulg Deathcheater quickly looks to invoke the blessings of the Great Maw, casting spells to disrupt ranged enemies or rival spellcasters. 

## **At Ease**
Matthogg’s camp is full of nervous energy, as most of his troops are earnestly considering if his leadership is still in their best interests. In the brief window after a sizeable meal during which Ogres are somewhat satisfied, the denizens of the camp can be found exchanging stories of their past exploits, engaging in eating contents (when supplies allow), or betting on organised bouts of wrestling. 

Should the Characters come to blows with Matthogg’s Payswords, the mercenaries fight to very nearly the last Ogre standing, certain to the end that their natural strength and fortitude will prevail — in the experience of most Ogres, it usually does. If the Characters are captured, they are given a brief opportunity to beg for their lives before being told ‘Don’t be late for dinner, eh?’ and handed over to the company’s Butcher. 

## **Settling a Debt**
## **Easy Encounter**
Skel Longstrider has been making a name for herself in nearby inns and amongst travellers on the road. Loudly boasting of her involvement in the Backbreaker tribe’s illegal tolls, several merchants have banded together and offered a bounty to anyone who can convince Matthogg’s camp to move elsewhere. The merchants are convinced that the Ogres will soon start extorting payments in much the same way they did near Altdorf; if Skel has her way, they may well be correct. 

Still, no one has claimed the bounty as of yet or even made a serious attempt to convince the Ogres to go elsewhere. There are almost a dozen mercenaries at the camp east of Nagenhof, and few have the nerve to face even a lone Ogre head-on, let alone demand anything of a camp of them. Thus, the amount on offer has only risen and currently stands at some 100 Gold Crowns. Of course, if the Ogres discover there is money to be made simply by moving away, they may attempt to claim the bounty themselves. Quite what will happen if they make a habit of this everywhere they stop is anyone’s guess. 

MATTHOGG’S PAYSWORDS 

## **Runic Indigestion Medium Encounter**
The Dwarf runes Rulg Deathcheater devoured still reside in his gut, their preservative magics causing them to act like arcane bezoars in the Ogre’s massive gut. This has caused Rulg to be able to extract much more magic from the artefacts he consumes, and his powers have grown appreciably since he first swallowed the ancient carved stones. These runestones were originally used to instruct apprentice Runesmiths, and each is a perfect example of Dwarf crafting. They are revered by the Runesmiths of Zhufbar, where their loss is considered a terrible tragedy. 

The three former Loremasters who still pursue Rulg are Bardun Oakheart, Brunna Nokinsdottir, and Dorek Halfhand. They have hunted the Butcher for years, always close but never quite catching up with their prey. They think Rulg is incredibly canny for an Ogre, though in fact his ability to evade them may have more to do with the Rune of Fate he ate that occasionally grants him prophetic dreams. The trio have come across many of Rulg’s camps, and suffered the indignity of checking through the Ogre’s middens to see if any contain a Runestone the Butcher may have passed. To say that they are livid, even for Slayers, is something of an understatement. 

The Slayers have at last discovered the location of Rulg’s camp. While they would love nothing more than to rush straight in and start hacking, even the three Slayers know they would fare poorly against an entire Ogre Mercenary company — the Slayers’ severely reduced numbers are proof enough of that. The trio sent word to Karak Kadrin, but in the meantime have cast about at every nearby inn and crossroads for suitable brave folks to assist them. 

So far, none have taken up their offered reward of ‘Glory and the thanks of all the Dwarfs of the Grey Mountains’ — a touch abstract for the average mercenary. However, this offered reward is no boast. While the Slayers have barely two shillings to rub together, any who aided in the recovery of the runestones would indeed be considered a friend of the Dwarfs and perhaps even be granted a runic weapon or suit of armour of their own. 

## **Belch and Slurry Hard Encounter**
The Payswords’ remaining Mournfangs are more trouble than they are worth to feed, and the company has taken to releasing them in remote parts of the forest to hunt. While the Ogres consider the beasts domesticated and essentially harmless, they have in fact reaped a bloody swathe across the vicinity. Locals refer to them as the ‘Twin Terrors’, and tales of their depredations are told in every nearby inn and coaching house. In fact, even Matthogg has heard of the bounties offered for the beasts’ heads and has sent parties of Ogres to search for them. He doesn’t realise the beasts are his own errant Mournfangs. 

Yrg Beastkiller is fond of the pair and has realised just which beasts the offered bounties are for. The Mournfangs remind her of home, and she is worried that they will eventually be tracked down and killed. If anyone is to kill them, she would rather it was her. To avoid their loss, she has taken to following bands of hunters who come looking for the creatures. Any who draw close to the Mournfangs’ hunting grounds are driven away (Yrg tells them she is there to hunt the creatures herself), or killed if they refuse to leave. 

Unfortunately for her, Gregor Hornstadt, a trapper from Nagenhof, escaped her most recent ambush and is recuperating in an inn near Bechafen. He is seeking revenge and promises to lead any who wish to the hunting grounds of the Twin Terrors. He claims this is to win the bounty on the Terrors, though, in fact, he hopes to find Yrg again and take her by surprise with whatever force of dangerous-looking people he can muster. He’s not too picky — after all, he can always escape and recruit a new group if things take a bad turn. 

## A Bellyfull of Trouble
The Payswords could potentially come into conflict with a number of different forces. The presence of Ogres in the Empire is usually tolerated, though not without strain. Even those Ogres who are most used to Human contact still occasionally find it tempting to consume fresh corpses and the occasional farm hand. The rulers of Ostermark will only brook a few tales of the Ogres’ depredations before deciding to move them on. However it is the growing dissatisfaction of the nearby Forest Spites that ought to concern Matthog. Small but powerful beings with an array of magical tricks at their disposal could make for a surprisingly tough opponent to the big brutes on their forest’s edge. 

## **Matthogg – Ogre Bruiser**
Matthogg is a veteran campaigner, having taken part in countless battles since he left the Ogre Kingdoms decades ago. His combat experience began long before that, however. Matthogg had made a name for himself as a brutal warrior and voracious eater, even by Ogre standards, even before he left the mountains. 

His long years among the ‘Slims’ (as Ogres invariably call members of every other species) have granted him a better than average understanding of Human concepts such as laws and reliable wages, as well as the terrible fuss they make when you devour something, or someone, that isn’t yours to eat. Thus, he prefers to avoid violence he is not paid to partake in, often repeating the mantra ‘If you’re good at something, never chew it for free.’ This makes Matthogg notably patient and reserved for an Ogre. 

Of course, if Matthogg believes that there is good cause for violence, he will not hesitate to join in. A flash of gold, and the promise of more to come, garners his attention. Any who go down this path should be prepared for the rather enormous fees Ogre mercenaries expect to be paid.

## **Rulg Deathcheater – Ogre Butcher**
Rulg was indoctrinated into the worship of the Great Maw in much the same way as a great many Butchers before him — taught the ways of endless hunger and feasting, and ultimately of extracting the magic present in flesh. Where most Ogres yearn for the taste of meat, however, Rulg longed for the taste of magic itself. He has travelled far and wide for decades, devouring shamans, wizards, and magical beasts wherever he could get them. 

Even ordinarily inedible objects infused magic satisfy Rulg’s hunger — if only for a moment. He has devoured grimoires, magical weapons and armour, as well as an entire collection of Dwarf runestones struck before Sigmar Heldenhammer ever walked the Old World. He earned the name ‘Deathcheater’ some years after this final exploit. An entire cadre of Dwarf Slayers, made up of the library’s Loremasters who had taken the Slayer’s Oath after the loss of the Runestones, chased him across most of the Border Princes. At least three search for Rulg still.

## **Yrg Beastkiller – Ogre Hunter**
Yrg is the most accomplished of the Payswords’ Hunters. Her javelins are carved of hardwood and as thick as a stout Dwarf ’s arm. They function both as a hunting weapon and as a spit for cooking — often one quite quickly after the other. Yrg joined up with the Payswords in search of great beasts to slay, and while she has had the opportunity to hunt some truly unusual creatures, all have paled in comparison to the creatures of her homeland. 

Bereft of fresh hunting grounds and frustrated at Matthogg’s refusal to move on, Yrg has taken to raiding nearby farms for meat, disguising her kills by giving them a brief stomping. She claims it is ‘To tenderise ‘em. Real stringy meat on these bones, boss’, which has annoyed the Butcher Rulg no end, as that is clearly part of his duties. 

It is only a matter of time until her forays draw attention from the law, but Yrg sees this as advantageous. Either no one stops her ‘hunting’ trips to the nearby farms, in which case the Payswords continue to eat, or a brief and fulfilling tussle with some local road wardens will convince Matthogg to adopt more aggressive tactics.

## **Skel Longstrider – Ogre Irongut**
Skel is a recent addition to Matthogg’s warband. Before joining him, she travelled with the Backbreaker tribe, which last year set up camp just a few miles north of Bechafen. The clan Tyrant had the idea of establishing a toll on the road to Wolfenburg road, and initially managed to extract a great deal of gold in the process. Delighted with the sudden apparently endless availability of coin, food, and drink, the Ogres of the Backbreaker tribe were busy congratulating themselves for their genius when a squadron of Knights of the Osterknacht descended on their camp and drove them back into the mountains. 

All this would be fine, were Skel discreet enough to keep her involvement a secret. Instead, she loudy tells anyone who will listen of her exploits, and more than once has greeted a merchant she recognised from the shakedown like an old friend. 

Skel is convinced that such a scheme could work again, and has been working to convince Matthogg of the same. The mercenaries grow desperate, and perhaps soon enough, Skel knows, it may not matter if Matthogg agrees or not…

## **Gut Magic**
Sometimes known as Shamanic Victuals, Gastromancy, Thaumaphagy, or Corpomancy, Gut Magic is a series of shamanistic rites involving the consumption of particular ingredients to channel the power of the Great Maw. The Lore of The Great Maw is detailed in **Archives of the Empire Volume 2** . These additional spells are used by Rulg Deathcheater and may also be learned by Ogre Characters who use the Lore of the Great Maw. 

## **Get Some Guts**
## **Cn:** 6
## **Range:** You
**Target:** Ogres within AoE (Willpower Bonus Yards) 

**Duration:** Willpower Bonus Rounds 

The Butcher consumes the large intestine of a male Mournfang. For the duration of the spell any targets may ignore _Broken_ Conditions. 

## **Toothcracker**
Whenever an Ogre Butcher successfully casts a spell from the Lore of The Great Maw, the offering they consume may restore their health. Roll 1d10. If the result is a 10, or if it is equal to or higher than the CN of the spell being cast, the Butcher recovers Wounds equal to the CN. 

When Butchers suffer a miscast they do not roll on the normal miscasts table. Instead, roll 1d100 on the Gut Magic Miscast Table on the facing page. If the miscast is a Major Miscast, add 20 to the roll. 

## **Bilebrew**
## **Cn:** 6
**Range:** You 

## **Cn:** 8
## **Range:** You
**Target:** AoE (Willpower Yards) 

**Duration:** Willpower Bonus Rounds 

The Butcher grinds his way through a lump of earthencrusted bedrock taken from the peak of a mountain, imbuing themself and their charges with supernatural resilience. The Butcher must take a **Challenging (+0) Endurance** Test, and if they fail they lose 1 tooth for every –1 SL they score on the test. If the spell is cast successfully, the Butcher and all friendly Ogres within the Area of Effect benefit from +20 to any Endurance and Cool Tests they are called on to make, and +1 AP to all Hit Locations, for the duration of the spell. 

**Target:** AoE (Willpower Bonus Yards) 

**Duration:** Willpower Bonus Rounds 

The Butcher knocks back an acrid concoction of spleen and gall, causing other Ogres nearby to attack their enemies with a cold fury and bitter determination. If the spell is cast, the Butcher and all friendly Ogres within the Area of Effect develop _Hatred_ against a target (or group of targets) of the Butcher’s choice. 

## Ingredients and Gut Magic
Unlike most other forms of magic, Gut Magic requires ingredients. These ingredients are mentioned in the description of the spell. The ingredients do not provide any additional benefit to spellcasting, such as mitigating miscasts, they are simply needed to make the spell work, and a Butcher without ingredients may not work Gut Magic. 

## **Bloodgruel**
**CN:** 5 

**Range:** You 

**Target:** You 

**Duration:** Instant 

The butcher places a disembodied limb into trheir mouth and sucks out all the blood and marrow. As the Butcher gulps down the cocktail of juices, their gut gurgles with magical energy, either healing them or, if the maw is displeased, ravaging their insides. If the spell is cast, the Butcher should make an **Easy (+40) Endurance** Test. If the test is passed, the Butcher heals 1 Wound plus 1 Wound for every +1 SL scored on the test. If the test is failed, the Butcher contracts the Bloody Flux. 

Several further Gut Magic Spells are included in **Archives of the Empire Volume 2** . They are _Bonecrusher, Bullgorger, Braingobbler, Feast of the Fallen, The Maw, Taste Death,_ and _Troll Guts_ .
